```{python}
#| label: ludb-semiseg-setup
import pandas as pd
from live_results import *

EVAL_DB = source_path("results/semiseg_ludb/semiseg_ludb.sqlite")
TRAIN_DB = source_path("results/semiseg_ludb_training/semiseg_ludb_mt_evaluation.sqlite")

def semiseg_tables(path, source):
    runs = read_sql(path, "select * from runs")
    if not runs.empty:
        runs = pd.concat([runs.drop(columns="summary_json"),
                          json_normalize(runs.summary_json, "metric.")], axis=1)
        runs["source"] = source
    streams = read_sql(path, "select * from stream_metrics")
    boundaries = read_sql(path, "select * from boundary_metrics")
    if not streams.empty: streams["source"] = source
    if not boundaries.empty: boundaries["source"] = source
    return runs, streams, boundaries

er, es, eb = semiseg_tables(EVAL_DB, "evaluation package")
tr, ts, tb = semiseg_tables(TRAIN_DB, "mean-teacher package")
runs = pd.concat([er, tr], ignore_index=True)
streams = pd.concat([es, ts], ignore_index=True)
boundaries = pd.concat([eb, tb], ignore_index=True)
```

## Provenance and completed runs

```{python}
#| label: ludb-semiseg-runs
display(source_inventory({"LUDB semiseg": EVAL_DB, "LUDB mean-teacher": TRAIN_DB}))
display(runs.sort_values(["source", "run_id"]))
display(runs.groupby(["source", "status", "split", "state_name", "padding"], dropna=False)
        .size().rename("runs").reset_index())
```

The two databases contain nine and seven completed run rows respectively.
Student and EMA states, padding choices, and dataset splits remain explicit;
they are not averaged into a single headline number.

## Stream-level region and interval metrics

```{python}
#| label: ludb-semiseg-streams
summary = (streams.groupby(["source", "run_id"])
           .agg(streams=("record_id", "size"), miou_mean=("miou", "mean"),
                miou_p05=("miou", lambda x: x.quantile(.05)),
                p_iou=("p_iou", "mean"), qrs_iou=("qrs_iou", "mean"),
                t_iou=("t_iou", "mean"), pr_error_ms=("notebook_pr_error_ms", "mean"),
                qrs_error_ms=("notebook_qrs_error_ms", "mean"),
                qt_error_ms=("notebook_qt_error_ms", "mean"))
           .reset_index())
summary = summary.merge(runs[["source", "run_id", "split", "state_name", "padding",
                              "checkpoint_sha256", "evaluator_sha256",
                              "metric.protocol", "metric.tolerance_ms",
                              "metric.evaluation_window"]],
                        on=["source", "run_id"], how="left")
display(summary)

# Boundary tolerance changes event matching but not region/interval predictions.
# Collapse exact performance duplicates before ranking those endpoints.
performance_columns = ["miou_mean", "miou_p05", "p_iou", "qrs_iou", "t_iou",
                       "pr_error_ms", "qrs_error_ms", "qt_error_ms"]
canonical_streams = summary.drop_duplicates(
    subset=["source", "checkpoint_sha256", "evaluator_sha256", "split",
            "state_name", "padding", *performance_columns]).copy()
display(leaderboard(canonical_streams, numeric_metrics(canonical_streams), id_col="run_id",
                    group_cols=("source",), k=10))
```

Two pairs of test rows have identical region and interval metrics because only
the event-matching tolerance changed. They remain in the provenance ledger but
are collapsed for region/interval ranking. Otherwise the same prediction set
would be counted twice as independent evidence.

## Boundary event accounting

```{python}
#| label: ludb-semiseg-boundaries
event = (boundaries.groupby(["source", "run_id", "boundary"])
         .agg(reference_events=("reference_events", "sum"),
              predicted_events=("predicted_events", "sum"),
              true_positive=("true_positive", "sum"),
              false_positive=("false_positive", "sum"),
              false_negative=("false_negative", "sum"))
         .reset_index())
event["sensitivity"] = event.true_positive / (event.true_positive + event.false_negative)
event["ppv"] = event.true_positive / (event.true_positive + event.false_positive)
event["f1"] = 2 * event.ppv * event.sensitivity / (event.ppv + event.sensitivity)
display(event)
```

These delineator results evaluate the LUDB semi-supervised component itself.
They are not reconstruction-model results and must not be used to rank ECG-AIM
checkpoints without the corresponding reconstruction inference protocol.

## Student-versus-EMA contrasts

```{python}
#| label: ludb-semiseg-ema-contrasts
ema_pairs = canonical_streams.pivot_table(
    index=["source", "checkpoint_sha256", "evaluator_sha256", "split", "padding"],
    columns="state_name", values=performance_columns).dropna().copy()
ema_delta = pd.DataFrame(index=ema_pairs.index)
for metric in performance_columns:
    if (metric, "model") in ema_pairs and (metric, "model_ema") in ema_pairs:
        direction = metric_direction(metric)
        sign = -1 if direction == "min" or metric.endswith("error_ms") else 1
        ema_delta[metric] = sign * (ema_pairs[(metric, "model_ema")] -
                                    ema_pairs[(metric, "model")])
display(ema_delta.reset_index())
```

EMA effects are small and mixed relative to evaluator effects. On the v1 valid
split, EMA raises foreground mIoU by 0.0021; on the v2 mean-teacher validation
checkpoints, changes are generally around one to three thousandths. Interval
errors do not improve uniformly—PR error can worsen while QRS/QT improve.
Therefore, “EMA is the better delineator” is not established as a universal
claim; state selection should remain split- and endpoint-specific.

## Padding and evaluation-window sensitivity

```{python}
#| label: ludb-semiseg-padding
padding_pairs = canonical_streams.pivot_table(
    index=["source", "checkpoint_sha256", "evaluator_sha256", "split", "state_name"],
    columns="padding", values=performance_columns).dropna().copy()
padding_delta = pd.DataFrame(index=padding_pairs.index)
for metric in performance_columns:
    if (metric, "none") in padding_pairs and (metric, "notebook") in padding_pairs:
        sign = -1 if metric.endswith("error_ms") else 1
        padding_delta[metric] = sign * (padding_pairs[(metric, "notebook")] -
                                        padding_pairs[(metric, "none")])
display(padding_delta.reset_index())
```

For the v1 test checkpoint, notebook padding changes foreground mIoU from
0.594 to 0.840 and reduces QT interval error from 30.45 to 11.34 ms—far larger
than the EMA effect. This is not evidence that padding makes the learned model
intrinsically better. It shows that temporal alignment and the evaluation
window are part of the estimand. The v2 `annotated` window was introduced to
make this contract explicit.

In the mean-teacher test package, notebook padding produces a smaller change
(foreground mIoU 0.775 to 0.783), with the largest benefit in P-wave overlap and
interval errors. Results from `none`, `notebook`, legacy v1, and annotated v2
must not be pooled into a single model leaderboard.

## Wave-specific failure structure

Across the v2 mean-teacher test runs, QRS IoU is approximately 0.84, whereas
P-wave IoU is about 0.67–0.71 and T-wave IoU about 0.80. QRS timing errors are
roughly 8–9 ms, while PR and QT errors remain larger. The principal residual
weakness is therefore atrial morphology and interval construction rather than
QRS localization. A headline mIoU obscures that imbalance.

## Semi-supervised claim ledger

| Claim | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| EMA universally improves delineation | Not supported | Effects are small, split-dependent, and mixed across interval endpoints. |
| Notebook padding is a model improvement | Incorrect interpretation | It changes alignment/evaluation support and can dominate apparent model effects. |
| Tolerance-20 and tolerance-150 rows are independent region results | No | They reuse identical predictions; only boundary matching changes. |
| QRS is the main failure mode | Contradicted | QRS overlap/timing are strongest; P-wave and interval endpoints are weaker. |
| These results rank ECG-AIM reconstructions | No | They evaluate the delineator component on native LUDB streams. |
| A canonical result can be reported | Yes, with contract | Checkpoint, state, split, padding, evaluator hash, window, and tolerance must all be named. |

## Remaining inferential limits

The databases contain a small number of checkpoint/state evaluations rather
than replicated training seeds. Stream observations are clustered within 40
subjects, but the summary tables do not provide subject-bootstrap confidence
intervals for student-versus-EMA or padding contrasts. Differences here are
descriptive engineering evidence until repeated training and subject-level
paired inference are added.
